title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — Tempe herbarium packet and selective conversion into models
scope_note: This is a minimum packet reconstructed from currently indexed Harvard University Herbaria search results, not a complete inventory of all Ganong-Blaschka collections at Tempe. Every row below is independently visible in HUH metadata. Further collector-level export/search may enlarge the packet.

minimum_packet_summary.interpretive_result: The Tempe collecting episode is already demonstrably broader than a model-production shopping list. The herbarium packet retains several taxa for which the current model/shipment corpus yields no exact species match, while one taxon, Hoffmannseggia, later branches into a glass descendant.

analytical_claim: Field collecting and glass manufacture were coupled through selective reference lineages, not by a one-specimen-to-one-model pipeline. A local collecting packet could preserve multiple botanical references at Harvard while only some references were later reactivated as glass models, sometimes after a substantial delay.
important_negative_evidence_rule: Treat absence from the current model list as an exact-string negative only. Historical synonymy, withdrawn models, unpublished workshop studies and missing labels can create false negatives. Upgrade a row to 'no model descendant' only after synonym and model-label checking.
comparison_with_model_345: Abronia umbellata differs structurally from the Tempe herbarium packet. Rudolf directly reports seeing it in the late-April western landscape and model 345 was shipped in February 1893, while no indexed Ganong-Blaschka Harvard herbarium sheet has yet been found in the present search. This suggests that model-relevant field reference could be retained through a drawing or observation pathway without requiring a surviving herbarium sheet.
next_steps: Find or derive a collector-level HUH search/export for W. F. Ganong & R. Blaschka and reconstruct the complete 1892 herbarium corpus with date and locality.

Run historical-synonym checks for Acmispon maritimus, Erodium cicutarium, Daucus pusillus, Cryptantha maritima, Brassica nigra and Lycium fremontii against all Harvard model labels and Blaschka shipment lists.
Inspect the nine HUH sheet images, prioritizing GH 01676890 and repeated Eriogonum inflatum sheets for handwritten collection/field annotations.

Compare day-level Tempe collecting dates with Rudolf/Ganong itinerary correspondence to determine whether the packet represents repeated local collecting, teaching exchange, or deliberate reference accumulation.
Keep this packet off the public route map until collector-level completeness and synonym checks are done; use it first as an argument about selective conversion of field references.
